label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §2.4…: EXPRESSIVISM_2: a moral sentence means the same in…
locator: §2.4, 'Such expressivists hold that the meanings of all sentences containing moral terms are determined by the mental states that they serve to express.'
interpretation: Expressivists in the narrower sense 'construct a systematic semantics for moral sentences by pairing them with the states of mind that the sentences are said to express'. The state a sentence serves to express belongs to the sentence, not to an occasion of use, so read as: a moral sentence means the same in every kind of occurrence. This is the second reading of 'meaning is expressing an attitude', beside SEP-MORAL-COGNITIVISM-4-1-EMOTIVIST-MEANING-OCCASION-A; §4.1 names it as the expressivist's way out ('Perhaps it might be some predictable function of this attitude'). Only constancy of meaning is formalized. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
